# Mutually active display update issue (2026-01-23 18:03Z)

_**User**_

when a route is ongoing and both devices had been "mutually active" it seems that, if one device stops requesting the location of the other device the "mutually active" display does not disable on its own. Only ever if the user switches tabs or restarts navigation it updates, could that be?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_


Investigating why the "mutually active" display doesn't update when one device stops requesting location. Searching the codebase for the "mutually active" logic and how it's updated.

        "contents": "    private func updateTrackingMode() {\n        let state = UIApplication.shared.applicationState\n        let status = locationManager.authorizationStatus\n        debugLog(\"updateTrackingMode called, state: \\(state.rawValue), status: \\(status.rawValue), isTracking: \\(isTracking)\")\n        switch status {\n        case .authorizedAlways, .authorizedWhenInUse:\n            if isTracking {\n                if state == .active {\n                    startHighAccuracyUpdates()\n                } else {\n                    startSignificantChangeUpdates()\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Ensure updates are stopped but preserve user's tracking preference flag\n                stopHighAccuracyUpdates()\n                stopSignificantChangeUpdates()\n            }\n        case .notDetermined:\n            // Do not reset isTracking while the user has not decided yet\n            break\n        case .denied, .restricted:\n            // Explicitly stop tracking if permission is denied/restricted\n            stopTracking()\n            // Update the setting to reflect the actual permission state\n            if settings.trackAndReportLocation {\n                settings.trackAndReportLocation = false\n            }\n        @unknown default:\n            stopHighAccuracyUpdates()\n            stopSignificantChangeUpdates()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func startHighAccuracyUpdates() {\n        debugLog(\"Calling startHighAccuracyUpdates\")",

        "contents": "    private func updateMutualState(targetDeviceId: String) {\n        // Find the newest visitor entry for the target device\n        let targetVisits = cachedVisitorHistory.filter { $0.DeviceID.uppercased() == targetDeviceId.uppercased() }\n        guard let newestVisit = targetVisits.max(by: { $0.TimeStampDate &lt; $1.TimeStampDate }) else {\n            // No visits from target device, not mutual\n            isMutualNavigation = false\n            return\n        }\n        \n        let age = Date().timeIntervalSince(newestVisit.TimeStampDate)\n        \n        // Hysteresis: different thresholds for enter/exit\n        if isMutualNavigation {\n            // Currently mutual: exit if age &gt;= T_exit\n            isMutualNavigation = age &lt;= tExit\n        } else {\n            // Not currently mutual: enter if age &lt;= T_enter\n            isMutualNavigation = age &lt;= tEnter\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "    private func formattedDistance(_ meters: CLLocationDistance) -&gt; String {\n        let usesMetric: Bool\n        if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.measurementSystem == .metric\n        } else {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.usesMetricSystem\n        }\n        let value: Double\n        let unit: UnitLength\n        if usesMetric {\n            value = meters / 1000.0\n            unit = .kilometers\n        } else {\n            value = meters / 1609.344\n            unit = .miles\n        }\n        let measurement = Measurement(value: value, unit: unit)\n        let formatter = MeasurementFormatter()\n        formatter.locale = .current\n        formatter.unitStyle = .short\n        formatter.unitOptions = .providedUnit\n        let numberFormatter = NumberFormatter()\n        numberFormatter.maximumFractionDigits = 0\n        numberFormatter.minimumFractionDigits = 0\n        formatter.numberFormatter = numberFormatter\n        return formatter.string(from: measurement)\n    }\n\n    private func transportSymbolName() -&gt; String {\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: return \"figure.walk\"\n        case 2: return \"car\"\n        case 3: return \"tram\"\n        default: return \"car\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func updateBottomAccessory() {\n        if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {\n            let visible = (travelTime != nil || distanceText != nil)\n            routeInfoState.update(\n                etaText: travelTime,\n                distanceText: distanceText,\n                transportSymbolName: transportSymbolName(),\n                visible: visible,\n                isMutualNavigation: mutualNavigationDetector.isMutualNavigation\n            )\n        }\n    }\n    \n    \n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * MutualNavigationDetector.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2026-01-19.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\nimport Combine\nimport MiataruAPIClient\n\n/// Detects mutual navigation state between two devices by polling visitor history.\n/// Implements hysteresis to avoid flickering (T_enter=60s, T_exit=90s).\nfinal class MutualNavigationDetector: ObservableObject {\n    @Published var isMutualNavigation: Bool = false\n    \n    private var targetDeviceId: String?\n    private let ourDeviceId: String\n    private var serverURL: String\n    private var pollingTimer: AnyCancellable?\n    private var cachedVisitorHistory: [MiataruVisitor] = []\n    private var lastPollTime: Date?\n    \n    // Hysteresis thresholds\n    private let tEnter: TimeInterval = 60.0  // Enter mutual state if last seen &lt;= 60s ago\n    private let tExit: TimeInterval = 90.0   // Exit mutual state if last seen &gt;= 90s ago\n    \n    // Polling interval (15-30s as specified)\n    private let pollingInterval: TimeInterval = 20.0\n    \n    init(ourDeviceId: String, serverURL: String) {\n        self.ourDeviceId = ourDeviceId\n        self.serverURL = serverURL\n    }\n    \n    /// Start monitoring for mutual navigation with the given target device.\n    /// Stops any existing monitoring.\n    func startMonitoring(targetDeviceId: String, serverURL: String? = nil) {\n        stopMonitoring()\n        self.targetDeviceId = targetDeviceId",

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

---


The issue: `MutualNavigationDetector` only calls `updateMutualState()` when the visitor history changes. If one device stops requesting, the history doesn't change, so the state isn't re-evaluated even though the last visit's age increases.

Checking the exact logic:


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="read_file_v2">
<details><summary>Tool use: **read_file_v2** • Read file: /Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/Common/MutualNavigationDetector.swift</summary>

</details>
</tool-use>

---


The issue: `updateMutualState()` is only called when the visitor history changes. When one device stops requesting, the history doesn't change, so the state isn't re-evaluated even though the last visit's age increases. We should always re-evaluate the state on each poll, not only when the history changes.

Updating the code to always call `updateMutualState()` after polling:


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="edit_file_v2">

</details>

</tool-use>

Fix complete. Summary:

## The Problem

The `MutualNavigationDetector` only re-evaluated the mutual navigation state when the visitor history changed. When one device stopped requesting the other's location, the history didn't change, so the state wasn't re-evaluated even though the last visit's age increased.

## The Solution

1. Always re-evaluate state after each poll: `updateMutualState()` is now called on every successful poll, not just when the history changes. This ensures the state updates when the age of the last visit exceeds the 90-second exit threshold.

2. Handle errors: On fetch errors, still re-evaluate using cached data, since time continues to pass.

The "mutually active" display will now disable automatically when one device stops requesting location, without requiring tab switches or navigation restarts. The state is re-evaluated every 20 seconds (the polling interval), so it should update within that timeframe after the exit threshold is exceeded.

The "mutually active" display goes away when the last visit from the target device is 90 seconds or older.

From the code:
- Enter threshold: 60 seconds — enters mutual state if the last visit was ≤ 60 seconds ago
- Exit threshold: 90 seconds — exits mutual state if the last visit was ≥ 90 seconds ago

Hysteresis prevents flickering: it takes longer to exit (90s) than to enter (60s).

Since polling runs every 20 seconds, the display typically disappears within the next poll after 90 seconds have passed. Worst case: up to 110 seconds (90s threshold + 20s polling interval) from when the other device last requested your location.

With the fix, the state is re-evaluated on every poll, so it will detect when 90 seconds have passed and automatically remove the "mutually active" display.

Committed the changes. Summary:

## Commit Summary

**Commit:** `4f7764a` - "Fix mutual navigation state not updating when device stops requesting"

**Problem Fixed:**
The "mutually active" display didn't disappear when one device stopped requesting the other's location because the state was only re-evaluated when the visitor history changed. When requests stopped, the history didn't change, so the state wasn't updated.

**Solution:**
1. Always re-evaluate mutual state on every poll (every 20 seconds), not just when history changes. This ensures the state updates when the age of the last visit exceeds the 90-second exit threshold.
2. Also re-evaluate state on fetch errors using cached data, since time continues to pass even when network requests fail.

**Result:**
The "mutually active" display now correctly disappears within ~90-110 seconds after the other device stops requesting location, without requiring tab switches or navigation restarts.

The changes have been committed to the `history` branch.
